newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore launches regional share index.
newsitem.headline: Singapore launches regional share index.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Oct 15 (SES) - The Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) launched on Tuesday a share index for local and foreign companies listed in Singapore with substantial operations in the Asian region.
The Business Times Singapore Regional Index (BT-SRI) covers 38 stocks ranging from companies involved in shipyards, electronics, food, and finance to telecommunications.

Of the 38 stocks, 24 are quoted in Singapore dollars and 14 in U.S. dollars. Seven of the components are the foreign tranches of Singapore companies which have both local and foreign tranche listings.
A statement by the SES said the index would be weighted by market capitalisation. A factor weighing against manipulation of the index would be the size of the companies included.
"Firms of market capitalisation of at least US$200 million or Singapore $280 million are considered for the index," the statement said.

Launching the index, Singapore Minister for Finance Richard Hu said the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) would study its performance to evaluate the feasibility of introducing a futures contract based on it.

"A preliminary study has concluded that the SRI may be a more suitable candidate than the Straits Times Industrial Index (STII) to fashion a futures contract as unlike the STII, which is price-weighted, the SRI is a capitalisation-weighted index and is less susceptible to market manipulation," Hu said in a speech.
Hu also said six Singapore banks would jointly sponsor a unit trust which would invest exclusively in the SRI component stocks. The initial size for the fund for the unit trust would be S$50 million.

He said Singapore Press Holdings, owner of the Business Times newspaper and co-partner in the launch of the regional index, has made a commiment to report more extensively on the 38 component stocks in the index.
Hu said the SRI had been developed in response to calls from market participants for a benchmark to measure the performance of their investment portfolios in Asia.
"This reflects the increasing international dimension of the Singapore stock market," Hu said.
